note: Rabbi Yirmeya, or some say Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba, said that Onkelos the convert composed the Aramaic translation of the Torah from the teaching of Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua, and Yonatan ben Uzziel the translation of the Prophets from Haggai, Zechariah and Malachi. When Yonatan made his, the Land of Israel quaked and a Divine Voice asked: Who has revealed My secrets to mankind? Yonatan stood and said: I did, not for my honor or my family's, but for Yours, so that disputes would not multiply in Israel. He wished also to translate the Writings, but the Divine Voice said: Enough. The Gemara explains: they contain the end of days, when the Messiah comes.
why: The Gemara has just discussed letters the prophets restored, and cites another teaching of the same Sage. It then asks how Onkelos composed the Torah translation if it already existed in Ezra's day, and why the Prophets' translation shook the land when the Torah's did not.
